preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 100 and 1 <= m <= 100 for n, m in [(int(x) for x in stdin.split()[0:2])])
preconditions.description: The first line contains two integers n (number of flowers) and m (number of suggested subarrays), each between 1 and 100 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(-100 <= int(x) <= 100 for x in stdin.split()[2:2+n])
preconditions.description: The second line contains n integers representing flower moods, each between -100 and 100 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(l) <= int(r) <= n for line in stdin.splitlines()[2:] for l, r in [line.split()])
preconditions.description: Each of the next m lines contains two integers l and r (1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ n) representing a subarray from index l to r (1-based).
The input consists of exactly m + 2 lines: one for n and m, one for flower moods, and m lines for subarrays.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().isdigit() and int(stdout.strip()) == max(sum(a[i] * sum(1 for l, r in subarrays if l <= i+1 <= r for subarrays in [[(int(l), int(r)) for l, r in line.split()] for line in stdin.splitlines()[2:]] for i in range(n)) for a in [[int(x) for x in stdin.split()[2:2+n]]])
postconditions.description: The output is a single integer representing the maximum possible happiness value, computed as the sum over all flowers of (flower mood × number of chosen subarrays containing that flower). The chosen subarrays are any subset of the m suggested subarrays.
